title: rcisignal: a complete workflow for reverse-correlation data quality
text: rcisignal consolidates quality-assurance workflow reverse-correlation (RC) experiments one toolkit. addresses three questions, order. First, inputs clean (response coding, trial counts, response bias, stimulus- pool alignment)? Second, signal informative stable (condition’s group CI carry pattern chance, pattern replicate different half producers)? Third, one condition, conditions distinguishable, overall magnitude spatial location? code: sm <- res$signal_matrix tc <- setNames(rep(300L, ncol(sm)), colnames(sm))  # 1. Compare observed and reference norm distributions directly. iv  <- infoval(sm, noise_matrix, tc, iter = 1000L, seed = 1L) ref <- iv$reference[[as.character(tc[1])]] cat(sprintf(   "observed median = %.4f, reference median = %.4f, %% above = %+.1f%%\n",   median(iv$norms), median(ref),   100 * (median(iv$norms) - median(ref)) / median(ref) ))  # 2. Sanity-check the chance baseline.
